 The college football season continues on Wednesday with a showdown between Buffalo and Central Michigan at Broadview Stadium. The 7-3 Bulls (5-1 in the Mid-American Conference) welcome the 5-5 Chippewas (3-3 in MAC) to Amherst in the midst of their best run of regular-season form since 2022.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That was the last time Buffalo enjoyed a streak of five straight wins in the same regular season, with the Bulls hoping to end this season on double-digit victories for the first time since 2018 (including bowl game). Third-year head coach Pete Lembo has recovered from a poor start to the campaign and is now leading one of four teams tied on 5-1 records at the top of the MAC.
 Toledo – whom Buffalo beat on the road last month – currently holds the edge at the summit with a superior 8-2 overall record compared to its other peers. However, Buffalo can afford some confidence this regular season will end with a 9-3 record in tow, with a trip to face 1-9 Akron last to come after this week's final home fixture.
 The Bulls boast the best rushing talent in the MAC, with running back Messiah Burch sitting on 1,110 rushing yards and seven touchdowns this season – though receiver Chance Morrow leads the team with nine scores this term. That doesn't bode well for a Central Michigan defense that ranks 91st in the country against the rush (allowing 161.1 yards per game), while their pass defense ranks as one of the best (ninth) and gives up just 164.7 YPG to opposition quarterbacks.
